papers.title: Development of novel auxetic LPBF-produced Ti6Al4V metamaterials
papers.abstract: Abstract Mechanical (or structural) metamaterials are revolutionizing property tailoring, offering capabilities beyond conventional bulk materials to meet the demand for structural innovation. This work presents the design, fabrication, and characterization of a novel 2D Ti6Al4V mechanical metamaterial. Designed using a novel design methodology, the structure exhibits auxetic (negative Poisson’s ratio) behaviour within its elastic domain. The metamaterial was produced using laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), and its mechanical response was experimentally tested and validated against numerical simulations, both measuring a −0.15 Poisson’s ratio. Dimensional discrepancies, specifically a reduction in lattice strut thickness, were found to significantly affect structural stiffness. An initial 42% deviation between numerical simulations and experimental results was observed, however by calibrating the computer-aided design model to reflect the as-built geometry, this error was reduced to 5%, validating the predictive accuracy of this refined numerical approach. The findings demonstrate that LPBF is a viable and effective method for producing 2D Ti6Al4V mechanical metamaterials capable of achieving high elastic strain, validating the integrated design and manufacturing approach.

summary_en.motivation: To develop and characterize a novel Ti6Al4V auxetic metamaterial with negative Poisson's ratio.
summary_en.method: The metamaterial was fabricated via laser powder bed fusion and characterized through mechanical testing and finite element simulations.
summary_en.result: A Poisson's ratio of -0.15 was achieved, and calibration of the CAD model to as-built geometry reduced the deviation between simulation and experiment from 42% to 5%.
summary_en.validation: Experimental results were validated against numerical simulations with good agreement after geometry correction.

papers.title: Prediction of the insulin growth factor release capacity from polymeric carriers on additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V scaffolds using machine learning
papers.abstract: Electron beam powder bed fusion (EB-PBF) has produced Ti-6Al-4V scaffolds that show promise for bone engineering. The current study employed machine learning (ML) analyses on 60 samples of experimental polymeric carriers that contained insulin growth factor-1 (IGF-1) on Ti-6Al-4V scaffolds and applied their porous structure for enhanced drug transport. Important determinants were pore size, drug release mass, time, and carrier ratio. We systematically developed and evaluated two ensemble regression algorithms, the Gradient Boosting (GB) Regressor and the Random Forest (RF), using several statistical metrics, such as the coefficient of determination (R²), the root mean squared error (RMSE), the mean squared error (MSE), and the mean absolute error (MAE). Bayesian optimization methods were used to improve model generalization and robustness by optimizing hyperparameters. Among the models used, RF performed the best with an R² value of 0.87, signifying an excellent degree of agreement between predicted and experimental results and demonstrating symmetric error distribution for high reliability and resistance towards overfitting. This association between the scaffolds and machine learning will further advance drug stability and efficacy as well as controlled drug delivery technologies while making biomaterial development more efficient and data-driven.

summary_zh.method: 基于60个样本，采用梯度提升和随机森林回归模型，结合贝叶斯优化超参数。

summary_zh.validation: 通过统计指标（R²、RMSE等）评估模型，未进行机械性能验证。

summary_en.motivation: To employ machine learning for predicting insulin growth factor-1 release from polymeric carriers on additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V scaffolds.
summary_en.method: Gradient boosting and random forest regression models with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization were developed using 60 experimental samples.
summary_en.result: Random forest achieved the best performance with an R² of 0.87, indicating excellent agreement between predictions and experimental data.
summary_en.validation: Model validation relied solely on statistical metrics on the test set; no mechanical or fatigue testing was performed.

papers.title: Effect of TiC Heterogeneous Nucleation Site Particles on the Melting Behavior of Ti-6Al-4V Powder by <i>In-Situ</i> X-ray and Thermal Imaging during Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effects of TiC addition on the continuity and mass balance of Ti-6Al-4V powder under support-free conditions. The melting behavior was captured using in-situ imaging equipment. Then, the continuity, the mass of the melt track, and the mass of the spatters were measured via ex-situ observations. These values were compared with the melting behavior, and the relationships between them were revealed as follows: TiC addition improved the continuity of the melt track at a higher laser power and higher laser scanning speed under the present experimental conditions. Moreover, TiC addition increased the mass of the spatters, decreased the mass of the melt track, and increased the average temperature of the heated area under all experimental conditions. These changes are presumed to be induced by the increased energy absorption of the powder bed owing to the TiC addition. Subsequently, the mass of the spatters increased when more energy was distributed to vaporization owing to local heating. This led to an increase in the average temperature of the heated area and a decrease in the mass of the melt track. These insights can contribute to enhancing the determination of process parameters in the fabrication of not only porous and cellular metals but also common parts made of Ti-6Al-4V powder with TiC particles.

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the effect of TiC particles on the melting behavior of Ti-6Al-4V powder during laser powder bed fusion.
summary_en.method: In-situ X-ray and thermal imaging were used to capture the melting process, and ex-situ measurements quantified melt track continuity, mass, and spatter.
summary_en.result: TiC addition improved melt track continuity at high laser power and scanning speed, but increased spatter mass and decreased melt track mass under all conditions.
summary_en.validation: The findings were validated by direct experimental observations and mass measurements.
